youtube.title: 43 Soldiers Re-Enlisted. The Headline Was GTA 6 #Shorts
youtube.description:
Forty three soldiers signed up for at least two more years in the army. And the headlines were all about four days of video games.

At Fort Stewart, Georgia, a battalion of the 3rd Infantry Division offered soldiers who signed a re-enlistment contract (at least two more years) by November 14 a special four day pass, timed to the release of GTA 6. The idea came from an army career counselor. 43 of the 130 eligible soldiers chose the pass. The pass came on top of the usual incentives: many still received their standard re-enlistment bonuses, and one soldier received over $60,000.

So why did the pass steal the show? Temptation bundling: pair something you should do with something you want. In a study at a university gym (Milkman, Minson & Volpp, 2014), people who could only listen to gripping audiobooks at the gym went 51% more often than the control group at first; the effect faded over time.

So, what would you bundle?

Sources:
- Military Times (2026-08-19), Army unit offers 96-hour Grand Theft Auto binge as incentive for reenlisting: https://www.militarytimes.com/news/your-military/2026/08/19/army-unit-offers-96-hour-grand-theft-auto-binge-as-incentive-for-reenlisting/
- Stars and Stripes (2026-08-21), Army memo on the re-enlistment pass: https://www.stripes.com/branches/army/2026-08-21/armygrandtheftautomemo-22617421.html
- Axios (2026-11-19), GTA 6 deal, perks and bonuses: https://www.axios.com/2026/11/19/gta-6-deal-perks-bonus-army
- Task & Purpose, Army re-enlistment and GTA VI: https://taskandpurpose.com/culture/army-reenlistment-gta-vi/
- Milkman, Minson & Volpp (2014), Holding the Hunger Games Hostage at the Gym, Management Science 60(2): 283-299: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25843979/
